impact_assessment.why: ADR-195's schedule is exact but exponential: at 8+ items it falls back to the shortest tour and loses items, so the shipped capability stops exactly where DeadlineWorld can still be measured.

impact_assessment.risks: contract: internal helper and cap constant only, no CLI or default change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: probe readout extends to larger item counts; regression: standing T1/T2/T3 pins must stay byte-identical.
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first equivalence tests against brute force on seeded layouts up to 7 items, explicit 8-12 item collection tests, the full suite and aikit 5/5.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] plan: add an additive patience parameter to DeadlineWorld (default 40, pins unchanged), measure the 11-12 item family across patience 40/80/120, and test ADR-197's claim that the shrinking gap is a property of the reward rule rather than the scheduler; record ADR-198.

impact_assessment.why: ADR-197 measured a narrowing shipped-vs-ablation gap at 11-12 items and attributed it to DeadlineWorld's fixed patient-item slack, but never varied that slack, so the boundary claim is untested.
impact_assessment.benefits: A measured patience sweep separates a world-rule limit from a planner limit, restores a full-item win where the rule allows it, and turns ADR-197's boundary into evidence.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive optional world parameter with a fixed default, no shipped-task change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no persisted state changes; regression: every T6 pin at default patience must stay byte-identical.
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests at patience 80/12 items, explicit default-patience pin checks, the full suite and aikit 5/5.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] plan: add an additive deadline_visibility parameter to DeadlineWorld and a strict planner-side fill of unknown deadlines with a patient horizon (recorded as probe.deadline.assumed), so a partial deadline map still schedules the known urgent item; measure graceful degradation over visibility 1.0/0.75/0.5/0.25 and record ADR-199.

impact_assessment.why: ADR-195/197 record that a partial deadline map makes the planner abandon scheduling entirely, losing the urgent item even when its deadline is known; ADR-192 named partial observability as a source of headroom that had never been tested.
impact_assessment.benefits: The shipped rule keeps using known deadlines under partial observability; the patient-assumption scope is explicit in the probe; a measured visibility sweep shows where the assumption stops helping.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive world parameter and additive probe field, no CLI or declared-policy change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: no persisted state changes; regression: full-visibility behavior and every standing pin must stay byte-identical.
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests at 0.5 visibility, explicit full-visibility pin checks, a visibility sweep, the full suite and aikit 5/5.
